_note:
AUTHORED 2026-09-03 against V2, the Esper enchantment list. Zur is a TOOLBOX: the commander is free from the command zone and its attack trigger fetches an enchantment at MV<=3 straight onto the battlefield. NOTHING HERE DECLARES THAT TRIGGER, because the goldfish does not model it — `command_zone_reduction` reads a commander for cost reduction only. So every component below is a card the deck must DRAW, which is the only thing this simulation measures.

The two REQUIRED components are what the deck cannot function without: a repeating draw engine (this is a resource deck before it is anything else) and an answer (a bracket-3 pod on a turn-four clock kills it otherwise). `engine_online` is therefore P(both drawn by turn N).

The two ROUTES are the kills the deck can actually assemble from cards in hand. Commander damage is deliberately NOT a route: Zur never needs drawing, so a drawn-cards simulation cannot say anything about it.

READ THE ENGINE FIGURE AS A DESCRIPTION, NOT AS EVIDENCE OF A LIFT. The same hand writes this file and reads the number. Three defensible declarations of one ur-dragon list gave engine lifts of +0.007, -0.036 and +0.014 over the same 10,000 games, which is why `deck_branch.MEMBERSHIP_AXES` refuses these axes as branch objectives. This declares what the deck is made of; it does not prove the parts help.

UPDATED 2026-09-03 after the artifacts came out. The deck now runs ZERO artifacts: they are invisible to Zur, whose trigger reads enchantments only, and the equipment that remained was MV2 — outside even Urza's Saga's {0}-or-{1} fetch, so nothing could tutor them and the only way to see one was to draw it. Their jobs moved onto auras Zur CAN fetch.

UPDATED 2026-09-03 after a card-by-card slot audit. `Scour for Scrap` was counted here as a TUTOR while searching for an artifact card in a deck holding zero artifacts — a declared component that could not resolve. `deck-audit` now reports that class of card as a note (`_dead_searches`), measured against the whole fleet first: two earlier versions fired on 2-of-3 and 23-of-47 correct cards and were thrown away. Sorin of House Markov left with it — extort competes with holding up interaction, and its flip wants 3 life in a turn from a deck whose lifegain is incidental.

REWRITTEN 2026-09-03. The Demonic Consultation + Laboratory Maniac line is GONE from the deck and from here: it was the deck's only real kill and it was a two-card tutor-for-the-win, which the pilot rejected outright. In its place the two lines the deck is actually built to run — a commander-damage clock the commander fetches for itself, and a drain that Vito finally makes lethal rather than incremental.

targets.label: RESOURCE ENGINE drawn — a draw engine that keeps drawing
targets._why: The deck out-resources the table and then converts; without a repeating engine it is a pile of answers with nothing to answer toward. One-shot selection (Brainstorm, Preordain) is deliberately EXCLUDED — it smooths a hand, it does not refill one.

any_of: Tribute to Horobi // Echo of Death's Wail

targets.label: AN ANSWER drawn — spot removal, a sweeper or a counterspell
targets._why: The table plays at a turn-four clock and some seats hold hard lockout effects. A Zur deck that draws no interaction loses before its commander has attacked twice. Widened 2026-09-03: the engine block named this the bottleneck at 0.709 by turn three, and the fix is COUNT, not cost — eight of the original ten were already MV<=2.

targets.label: KILL — commander damage: a buff aura on Zur
targets._why: Zur is FREE from the command zone, so the only part of this line that has to be DRAWN is the aura — which is why commander damage was undeclarable until the clock existed. Ethereal Armor is +1/+1 per enchantment in a 44-enchantment deck; Daybreak Coronet adds +3/+3 and LIFELINK, which is what feeds the drain route below. Zur also fetches both himself, so this rate is a FLOOR: the commander assembles its own clock and the simulation cannot see that trigger at all.

targets.label: KILL — drain: a payoff plus something to feed it
targets._why: Rebuilt around Vito, which is the CONVERTER the deck was missing: lifegain becomes life loss at full value, so Daybreak Coronet's lifelink turns a connection into twice its damage. Marauding Blight-Priest hits every opponent for 1 on the same trigger, and the constellation pair turn each enchantment that lands into both. NOTE Exquisite Blood and Sanguine Bond are DELIBERATELY ABSENT — either would make this a two-card infinite, which is the thing the pilot rejected. Vito alone is a payoff, not a loop. NOTE ALSO the simulation still cannot see any of it: life loss and death triggers are unmodelled, so this measures the PIECES, never the kill. Underworld Coinsmith sits in the PAYOFF leg only: it is both a payoff and fuel, and leaving it in both let one draw satisfy an AND of ORs twice — the defect `_validate_shared_leg` exists to catch, and it caught it here.

any_of: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
Tribute to Horobi // Echo of Death's Wail

targets.label: RAMP drawn — an accelerant of any kind
targets._why: Context, not a component: the mana block already reports land drops directly.

targets.label: A TUTOR drawn
targets._why: Context. Tutor density is reported and never scored, and a tutor is only as good as the target it fetches — which is what the routes above are for.
